title: GeoFA - 2D layout pattern matching using deterministic finite automaton
problem: Layout pattern matching in chip design is computationally expensive, requiring search through millions of geometric patterns to verify design rules or identify specific structures. Commercial tools like Calibre are slow for complex pattern searches.
motivation: Deterministic finite automaton (DFA) provides an efficient theoretical framework for exact pattern matching with linear-time complexity, dramatically faster than brute-force geometric search.
method: GeoFA represents 2D layout patterns as a finite automaton—a state machine designed to recognize specific pattern sequences. This automaton can scan through a chip layout and identify matches more efficiently than brute-force geometric search, because it follows predefined recognition paths rather than trying all possible geometric comparisons. The pattern specifications are encoded as states and transitions in the automaton, so the machine knows exactly what to look for and how to recognize it.
key_novelty: GeoFA applies finite automaton theory to 2D layout pattern matching, representing patterns as state machines to efficiently recognize matches in chip layouts.
contributions: DFA-based framework for 2D layout pattern matching
Efficient pattern verification methodology for manufacturing rule checking
limitations: The approach may require significant preprocessing for complex pattern specifications, and real-world applicability depends on integration with existing EDA tool ecosystems.
